what: loopmmt.com went live as a clean public mirror on GitHub Pages — the first thing the world could open.
why: The methodology had spent months in a private repo; the site is the front door, and a front door only counts once it opens.
rejected: A self-hosted box path was scoped and set aside — GitHub Pages is the live serve-path; the box path is noted, not taken.
learned: The public site is a redacted MIRROR of the private canon, air-gapped by construction — content flows one way through a gate, never the private tree itself.
next: Wire the homepage to the live rooms and retire the under-construction state.

what: Seated a MAJOR.MINOR version counter in every footer — a deploy counter rendered at build time, mirroring the software versioning convention.
why: A public site with no version is a site you can't reason about over time; every deploy should be countable and every page should say which deploy it is.
rejected: Not applicable — this is the convention that makes the rest of the spine legible.
learned: The counter was seeded at 1.24 by back-filling 24 prior content deploys from the public repo log (26 commits minus 2 CNAME chrome ops). Deploys before the counter existed are real but not individually version-stamped — this ledger states that gap rather than inventing entries to fill it.
next: Bump the counter on every deploy from here; each bump is a waypoint.
flags: seed: 24 pre-counter deploys back-filled, not individually recorded

what: Shipped The Prompts — a page that shows the actual prompts behind the work — live for the first time.
why: People kept asking what you actually type. The honest answer is a page, not a paragraph.
learned: A feature isn't shipped until the public SHA proves it; the canonical site.version is reconciled to the public deploy, not asserted ahead of it.
next: Propagate the new page into the site navigation everywhere.

what: Propagated The Prompts into the site navigation and reconciled the machine-digest layer to match.
why: A live page nobody can navigate to is only half-shipped.
learned: Nav is not one edit — it lives across many pages and two machine-digest indexes; propagate all in one pass or the site lies about itself.
next: Catch the pages where nav still hadn't landed.

what: Fixed a navigation gap — the build-generated corpus and KP pages were missing the new Prompts link.
why: Byte-truth caught it: the live generated pages didn't carry the link even after the manual nav edit, because the builder regenerates them and drops hand edits.
rejected: Editing the generated HTML by hand — it reverts on the next build.
learned: A nav change on a build-generated page must land in the BUILDER, not the output. Edit the source of the fold, never its shadow — or the deploy silently reverts it. (This is a recurring scar; it earned its own note.)
next: Continue nav consistency work across the page family.

what: Deployed prompt embed-cards — the prompts mixed into the apps gallery as live cards.
why: The prompts and the apps they made belong next to each other; separated, each is less.
next: Unify the navigation label for the feature.
flags: record shows the WHAT; the why/rejected here are thin in the commit record

what: Unified the nav label to 'The Prompts' across 19 top-level pages and 2 builders, and regenerated the folded pages.
why: Operator ruling: one name for one thing. Inconsistent labels read as carelessness.
rejected: Leaving the older label in place on some pages — an inconsistent label is a broken promise about attention to detail.
learned: A label sweep is a 21-surface edit (19 pages + 2 builders); the builders are the load-bearing two, because they regenerate the rest.
next: Reconcile the counter and keep deploying.

what: Reconciled the canonical counter to 1.30 as a deploy stamp.
flags: a reconcile/stamp bump — the record carries the WHAT (a deploy stamp), not a distinct feature why

what: Reconciled the counter to 1.32 and refreshed the corpus map (a deploy seed). Version 1.31 has no separate recorded commit — the counter moved 1.30 to 1.32 in the record.
learned: The recorded spine is coarser than the number: some bumps reconcile more than one deploy, so a gap (no 1.31 commit) is honest, not missing data.
flags: gap: no separate 1.31 commit — counter reconciled 1.30->1.32

what: Reconciled to 1.33 and regenerated the site-root machine-digest to match the live deploy.
why: The AI-facing layer (llms.txt / index.json) has to track the human-facing site, or an AI handed the site reconstructs a version that no longer exists.
learned: The machine-digest is a fold, not a hand-kept file — regenerate it with every deploy so the machine door and the human door agree.
next: Fix the Résumé nav that lagged across generators.

what: Fixed Résumé navigation in all 4 page generators (two were 2 links behind) and regenerated corpus + KP pages.
why: The generated pages had drifted behind the hand-authored ones — the same builder-drop scar from v1.27, in a new spot.
rejected: Patching the output pages directly — reverts on rebuild (the lesson from v1.27, applied).
learned: Nav drift concentrates in the generators; when a link is added, check all four generators in the same pass, not just the pages you can see.

what: Reconciled to 1.35 with the name-on-résumé refinement and a refreshed machine-digest.
why: A résumé without a name on it is a draft; small, but it's the kind of detail the whole site's credibility rides on.

what: Deployed app-pages Slice 4 — moved 7 app pages from the private design tree into the public site tree, fixed asset refs and nav, and allowlisted the one shared script.
why: The app pages were referencing the private design/ tree, which the deploy gate correctly REFUSES; moving them into site/ gives them clean public URLs and passes the gate.
rejected: Serving pages that reach into the private design tree — the gate refuses it by design, and rightly.
learned: A public page may reference ONLY allowlisted design assets; a /design/<x> reference from a public page is gate-refused. Fit the page to the gate, don't weaken the gate.
next: Build the How It's Made system + page (this arc).

what: Shipped this very page — 'How This Site Is Made' — built by The Making, the system it describes. The page carries its own waypoint: the deploy that ships it is v1.37, and this ledger entry is that waypoint's entry.
why: Grok's north star: the site should not merely CLAIM the methodology works — it should be EVIDENCE it works. A page about how the site is made, made by a system that derives its facts from the site's own git record, is that evidence closing on itself.
rejected: Merging into the existing Receipts page (would dilute both tight artifacts); manufacturing 36 tidy waypoints from a counter that only records ~11 (would be a lie the page exists to refute).
learned: The page is a specimen of the system: DERIVE the facts (the spine), AUTHOR the why (this ledger), BIND every authored claim to a byte-truth pointer, and where the record has no why — say so, out loud, on the page.
flags: forward entry: authored at the moment it ships — record-rather-than-reconstruct
